summary.note: Only the EXTERNAL tests validate anything. Circular tests compare against values the model was normalised to and prove only that the scaling arithmetic is right; internal tests are round-trips; range tests check a constant against published bounds.

note: Tests 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 compare against numbers published or computed by others. Tests 8 and 9 are internal-consistency or range checks and are labelled as such.
Test 10 deliberately expects disagreement in a known direction: full-pool outlines should exceed a drawn-down measured surface.

tests.test: Lake Mead total open-water evaporation
tests.reference_source: Reclamation HDB 2017-2021 average (LCR Evaporation Report 2023, Table 7)
tests.note: Our figure uses a 2024-2026 measured surface; Reclamation's is a 2017-2021 average over a larger lake, so ours should read lower. Direction of the difference is the check.

tests.test: Lake Mohave total open-water evaporation
tests.reference_source: Reclamation HDB 2017-2021 with 2021 USGS coefficients (Table 8)
tests.note: Level held on a seasonal guide curve, so surface area is comparable between periods.

tests.test: Lake Mohave surface area
tests.reference_source: Reclamation LCRAS 2017-2021 average surface area (Table 9)
tests.note: Sentinel-2 water mask vs Reclamation's area-capacity tables: independent methods.

tests.test: Lake Mead solar capacity factor
tests.reference_source: Typical fixed-tilt utility PV capacity factor, US Desert Southwest (EIA/NREL range 0.19-0.23)
tests.note: Sanity check on the PVGIS resource model at these coordinates.

tests.test: Lake Powell solar capacity factor
tests.reference_source: Typical fixed-tilt utility PV capacity factor, US Desert Southwest (EIA/NREL range 0.19-0.23)
tests.note: Sanity check on the PVGIS resource model at these coordinates.

tests.test: Glen Canyon annual generation
tests.reference_source: WAPA CRSP 2026 fact sheet, average annual energy
tests.note: CIRCULAR: the hourly series is normalised to this published figure, so agreement is guaranteed. Retained only as a round-trip check on the scaling arithmetic.

tests.test: Hoover annual generation
tests.reference_source: Reclamation, Hoover Dam average annual generation ~4 TWh
tests.note: CIRCULAR: normalised to this figure. Round-trip check only.

tests.test: NEVP annual average day-ahead price (Lake Mead's node)
tests.reference_source: Computed independently from the raw OASIS pull for NEVP, full year 2024
tests.note: Round-trip test of the Int16 quantisation used to embed prices in the page. An earlier version of this test used 29.56, which is the mean over only the hours the older SP15 series also covered; the test correctly failed until the reference was put on the same 8,784-hour basis as the model.

tests.test: Evaporation saved, Mead at 3% coverage
tests.reference_source: Closed-form identity: coverage x suppression x rate x area
tests.note: Internal consistency, not external validation.

tests.test: FPV areal density
tests.reference_source: Published utility FPV gross density, roughly 80-160 MW/km2 depending on layout
tests.note: Range check on a constant, not a validation of any model output.

tests.test: Lake Mead evaporation depth vs LCRAS accounting
tests.reference_source: Reclamation LCRAS reservoir evaporation volume 2019-2024 over measured area
tests.note: Independent of the USGS flux campaigns: this reservoir's rate comes from measured eddy-covariance flux and owes nothing to LCRAS.

tests.test: Lake Mohave evaporation depth vs LCRAS accounting
tests.reference_source: Reclamation LCRAS reservoir evaporation volume 2019-2024 over measured area
tests.note: Independent of the USGS flux campaigns: this reservoir's rate comes from measured eddy-covariance flux and owes nothing to LCRAS.

tests.test: Lake Havasu evaporation depth vs LCRAS accounting
tests.reference_source: Reclamation LCRAS reservoir evaporation volume 2019-2024 over measured area
tests.note: CIRCULAR AND LABELLED AS SUCH. Havasu has no flux measurement, so its rate is itself an LCRAS volume divided by an area. Comparing it back against that quotient cannot fail. Retained only to show the arithmetic is consistent, and it validates nothing.

tests.test: Lake Mead OSM full-pool outline vs measured water
tests.reference_source: Sentinel-2 measured 2024-2026 mean
tests.note: OSM outlines are full pool and should read HIGHER than a drawn-down measured surface. Directional: full-pool outlines should exceed a drawn-down measured surface. Confirms the correct water body, not agreement. Enforced one-sided: measured water exceeding full pool would mean the mask is picking up water outside the reservoir, which a symmetric tolerance would have passed.

tests.test: Flaming Gorge fitted hypsometry extrapolated to full pool
tests.reference_source: Reclamation published full-pool surface area
tests.note: Storage-elevation hypsometry fitted only to operating-range data, then evaluated at full pool. Published full-pool area never enters the fit, so this is a genuine out-of-sample test. Mead and Powell are excluded: full pool sits 130 ft and 64 ft above any level in the record, so it is extrapolation rather than validation.
